newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel-Germany will meet three pct EMU criterion.
newsitem.headline: Waigel-Germany will meet three pct EMU criterion.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Monday that Germany would fulfil the three percent deficit criterion for European monetary union (EMU).
"Germany will meet the deficit criterion," Waigel said at a conference on EMU.
Waigel also said he believed France's new Socialist government would make efforts to qualify for Europe's single currency.
Waigel also said all nations would have the opportunity to become EMU members at the start. "Every nation has its chance," he said.
Germany has struggled to narrow a gaping budget shortfall to meet the EMU target of public deficits totalling no more than three percent of gross domestic product.

Waigel also spoke out against the idea that the introduction of a "weak" single currency could lead to a break in the partnership of his Christian Social Union (CSU) and Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU).

He also said he was "independent" in the recent spat between Kohl and Edmund Stoiber, the CSU chief and Bavarian premier who has demanded delaying EMU unless all participants meet strict fiscal targets.
